title: fix(cli,driver-sql): `os migrate plan` stops creating a database on a fresh project (#6743)
body:
Fixes objectstack-ai/objectstack#6743

## What was wrong

`os migrate plan` calls itself a dry run, and since #3917 it reports the boot-time create-table DDL and the artifact seed instead of performing them. The **open** was never covered: SQLite brings its file into existence at open, so a `plan` in a never-started project left a 0-table `.objectstack/data/objectstack.db` behind.

Reproduction on `origin/main` (fresh project, never started), exactly as the card specifies — both `ls` outputs quoted:

```
$ os build
  ✓ Build complete

$ ls .objectstack/data/
ls: cannot access '.objectstack/data/': No such file or directory

$ os migrate plan
  ℹ Database: …/fresh-proj/.objectstack/data/objectstack.db
  ℹ Examined 6 managed table(s).
  New (additive — created when you apply)
    + fresh_note [create_table, 9 column(s)]
    + sys_metadata [create_table, 23 column(s)]
    …
  ℹ 6 table(s) to create, 0 column(s) to add

$ ls -la .objectstack/data/
-rw-r--r-- 1 root root 4096 Aug  9 06:46 objectstack.db      ← the defect
```

## The feasibility check the ruling owed, run before any code

The `domain:cli` ruling made this a hard precondition:

> ⚠️ **Feasibility is unverified and the dev owes a check before writing code**: this only works if the schema-diff path can run against an absent/empty target without an open write handle. If it cannot — if `bootSchemaStack` needs a real handle to produce a plan at all — then fall back to A **and say so explicitly in the PR body**, including what you measured that ruled the better route out.

**Measured: feasible, and route A is not needed.** Running the same fresh project with the target forced to an in-memory database produced a plan body **byte-for-byte identical** to the one produced against a real empty file (diff over the normalised output: no differences), and created nothing on disk. The diff path does need a live handle — it introspects `sqlite_master` — but an in-memory handle is a live handle. A database with zero tables is exactly what a freshly created empty file is.

So the ruled route is what landed: same report, minus the file. Route A (refuse to plan on a fresh project) was **not** used anywhere.

## One measured deviation from the ruling's wording — please read this bit

The ruling's mechanism sentence was "**Open read-only**, and when the file does not exist, diff against an empty schema in memory." The second half is implemented exactly. The first half — flipping the **existing-file** open to `readonly: true` — was measured and **deliberately not done**, because it is counter-productive for this issue's own goal:

```
--- (c) WAL db, clean close, then readonly-open ---
    dir after clean close:     [ 't.db' ]
    readonly open OK; tables=  [ 'x' ]
    dir while readonly-open:   [ 't.db', 't.db-shm', 't.db-wal' ]
    dir after readonly close:  [ 't.db', 't.db-shm', 't.db-wal' ]   ← left behind
```

Opening an existing WAL database read-only **creates `-shm` and `-wal` and cannot clean them up on close** (a read-only connection may not checkpoint or unlink them). Today's read-write open removes both on a clean close. So a blanket read-only open would *add* two stray files on the existing-file path — the exact defect class this card exists to remove — while fixing none, since there was never a defect there: the file already exists, and #3917 already stopped that boot from writing DDL or seed rows.

The ruling's stated **target end state** is met in full: "`os migrate plan` on a fresh project prints the SAME plan it prints today, and leaves NO file behind." The existing-file path is left byte-identical to today on purpose, and this note is here rather than silent.

(For completeness: `fileMustExist: true` and `readonly: true` both refuse a missing file with `SQLITE_CANTOPEN` and create nothing — so neither can produce the report the ruling insists on keeping. The in-memory stand-in is what makes "same report, no file" possible at all.)

## What changed

A new **additive** driver capability, off by default, so no existing caller changes behaviour:

- `SqlDriverConfig.sqliteAbsentFile`: `'create'` (default, SQLite's own behaviour) or `'empty-in-memory'`.
- `resolveSqliteAbsentFileTarget()` in `@objectstack/driver-sql` is the **one** place the "does the target exist?" judgement is made. It lives in the driver, not the CLI — the two-places-drift objection that ruled out route B.
- Threaded as a **host-composition** option (`createDefaultDatasourceDriverFactory` → `DefaultDatasourcePlugin` → `createStandaloneStack` → `bootSchemaStack({ readOnlyProbe: true })`), sibling to the existing `dev` gate. Deliberately **not** an authorable `datasource.config` key: `SqliteConfigSchema` is strict, and a datasource must not be able to declare itself into never persisting.
- The driver keeps `this.config` pointing at the **declared** file while only its Knex instance holds `:memory:`, which is what preserves the `Database:` line. `sqliteFilename()` reports `null` for a redirected connection, which is what stops `ensureDatabaseExists()` from `mkdir`-ing the state directory and `applySqliteJournalMode()` from putting an in-memory database into WAL.
- `standalone-stack` skips its own host-side `mkdirSync` in the same case — creating `.objectstack/data/` is the other half of the write side effect.
- The dev native→wasm step-down resolves the same helper, so a step-down cannot create the file the caller declined to create.

`os migrate apply` deliberately does **not** set it. It boots with `deferSchemaDdl` too, but flushes the deferred DDL after confirmation, so it needs a real file — a test pins that the flag never becomes implied by `deferSchemaDdl`.

## After

```
$ ls .objectstack/data/
ls: cannot access '.objectstack/data/': No such file or directory

$ os migrate plan
  ℹ Database: …/fresh-proj/.objectstack/data/objectstack.db
  ℹ Examined 6 managed table(s).
  New (additive — created when you apply)
    + fresh_note [create_table, 9 column(s)]
    + sys_metadata [create_table, 23 column(s)]
    …
  ℹ 6 table(s) to create, 0 column(s) to add

$ ls -la .objectstack/data/
ls: cannot access '.objectstack/data/': No such file or directory
```

Plan body diff, before-fix vs after-fix: **identical**, including the `Database:` line naming the real path. `os migrate apply --yes` still creates the file and the six tables; a second `plan` then reads the real database and reports "Physical schema is in sync".

## Sibling drivers (the PM's assumption 1, checked)

`SqliteWasmDriver` and `TursoDriver` both `extends SqlDriver`, and both build their own Knex config via `toKnexConfig(...)` before calling `super(...)`. Neither carries `sqliteAbsentFile`, so neither can receive it and **neither changes behaviour**. `driver-turso`'s RemoteTransport is untouched. The only place the wasm driver is affected at all is the dev step-down inside `resolveSqliteDriver`, where it is now handed the resolved filename on purpose — pinned by a new test. No `driver-memory` / `driver-mongodb` files were touched (frozen per #5499).

## Tests

- `packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver-sqlite-absent-file.test.ts` — 9 cases: the helper's three dispositions, no file/`-wal`/`-shm`/directory created, config still names the declared target, existing files opened normally, default mode still creates, inert for `:memory:` and pg.
- `packages/cli/src/utils/schema-migrate.readonly-probe.integration.test.ts` — THE PIN, through the real `bootSchemaStack`: a fresh project has no `.objectstack/data/` at all afterwards (`.db`, `-wal`, `-shm`, plus a sweep of anything else dropped in `data/`); the pending-work set and the database label match a control boot that does create the file; and `apply`'s flush still lands in a real file.
- `packages/services/service-datasource/src/sqlite-driver-fallback.test.ts` — 3 new cases for the step-down.

**Reverse verification** — direction predicted before running, and it is the plain Red case. Neutering `resolveSqliteAbsentFileTarget` to always return the declared filename turned red exactly the tests that pin the NEW behaviour (driver 3 of 9; CLI `expected [ Array(1) ] to deeply equal []`, i.e. the stray `objectstack.db` reappearing, and `expected true to be false` on the data directory), while every test pinning UNCHANGED behaviour stayed green — including "apply keeps its file", which is correct: the fix does not touch that path.

Local: `driver-sql` 1140 passed, `service-datasource` 267 passed, `runtime` 1744 passed, `cli` 1047 passed; `typecheck` green on all four. Every `check:*` step enumerated from `.github/workflows/lint.yml` was run one by one — all pass.
